decision: chose luxury/editorial refined aesthetic for Subscribe button
reason: frontend-design skill mandates bold, distinctive direction. 'Receive dispatches from the frontier' positions this as exclusive editorial content — gold-on-dark evokes letterpress printing, high-end publishing, and material luxury. This contrasts sharply with generic SaaS newsletter signups.

decision: selected dark background palette (#0e0c08 deep, #1a1610 surface) with gold accents (#c8a84e family)
reason: Dark + gold is an editorial trope but executed with restraint — very dark background with subtle warm undertones, gold used sparingly as accent rather than gaudy. Avoids the overused purple-gradient trend. Gold gradient on button has 175deg angle for asymmetrical light catch.

decision: paired Playfair Display (display) with DM Mono (functional text)
reason: Playfair Display is a distinctive high-contrast serif that carries editorial gravitas without being default (avoids Inter/Roboto/Arial ban). DM Mono provides crisp functional contrast for overline, input, button, fine-print. Italic variant of Playfair used for emphasis word 'dispatches' to create visual hierarchy within title.

decision: added radial gradient ambient light + SVG fractal noise overlay
reason: frontend-design skill calls for atmosphere/depth instead of flat solid backgrounds. Radial gradients create a subtle spotlight effect behind the card. SVG feTurbulence noise at 3% opacity adds paper-like texture that prevents the dark background from feeling like a void.

decision: centered card with generous padding, 6px inner border accent
reason: Single-element composition demands breathing room. 3.5rem padding creates editorial whitespace. Inner ::before pseudo-element with faint gold border adds a second frame — a detail users may not consciously notice but contributes to the 'premium object' feel.

frontend-design skill says 'one well-orchestrated page load with staggered reveals creates more delight than scattered micro-interactions.' Card slides up, then overline → title → description → form → fine-print cascade in. Each element uses cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) for decelerating elegance.

decision: gold gradient button with pseudo-element shine layer + hover glow
reason: Button is the primary CTA. Three-layer construction: (1) linear gradient base with 175deg angle for metallic sheen, (2) ::before overlay with white→transparent→black gradient simulating embossed/gloss effect, (3) ::after blur glow that appears on hover. This is maximalist detail work on a single element — exactly the precision the skill calls for.

decision: hover lift + outer glow, active press scale(0.985), loading state with text swap
reason: Button needs three distinct interaction states. Hover: 1px lift + box-shadow gold glow. Active: subtle scale-down for tactile feedback. Loading: text swap to 'Sending...' + disabled state. All transitions use the same expo easing for cohesion.

decision: inline email input + button combo with no visible gap
reason: Newsletter context demands email capture before subscribe. Input and button share 52px height, input has border-right:none and button has border-radius on right only — they fuse into a single visual unit. This is more deliberate than two separate rounded rectangles.

decision: form swappable to success message via .success CSS class
reason: No page navigation. CSS display:none/.success toggle swaps form for italic success text. Minimal DOM manipulation, CSS-driven transition. The italic 'Welcome.' + delivery promise adds personality to what could be a generic 'Thank you'.

decision: fine-print with no-spam pledge + platform transparency (Buttondown)
reason: Conversion UX: naming the actual delivery platform reduces anxiety about unknown senders. 'Unsubscribe anytime with a single click' is specific, not boilerplate. Mono font at 0.6rem makes it legible but visually secondary.

decision: aria-label on input, form validation with visual error state, semantic HTML
reason: Production-grade means accessible. <article> landmark, aria-label for screen readers, HTML5 constraint validation with visual feedback (red border flash). Input checkValidity() before simulated submission.

decision: clamp() for responsive title sizing, min() for card width, cursor states, disabled attr
reason: Responsive without media queries. title uses clamp(2rem, 5vw, 2.8rem). Card width is min(520px, 90vw). Disabled button has cursor:wait and reduced opacity. All edge states covered.
